value.estimate: 2 days for a Rust validator with a fixture generator and a CI matrix
value.why: the engine is small and the harness is standard cargo plus actions; the expensive part is sourcing real payloads, which this project did not do

data_and_models.value: No model; a rule/classification engine over fixtures it generates itself. Nothing in the capture describes where the twelve vector definitions came from or how a missed vector would be discovered.

how_it_works.value: 100% Rust. Engine logic in src/cvm.rs and src/main.rs; src/bin/gen_fixtures.rs generates clean and malicious fixtures; tests/simulation_matrix.rs runs the twelve scenarios; .github/workflows/test.yml provisions a runner, caches dependencies, compiles and executes the whole suite per change.

how_they_tested.value: A real harness is described - a fixture generator plus a twelve-scenario matrix executed by CI on every commit - which is the right shape for this kind of validator. But the page links no repository, workflow or run id, so the green-checkmark claim cannot be checked, and a suite whose cases and fixtures are both authored by the system measures agreement with itself.

limits_they_disclosed.value: The whole framework was written and committed from a mobile device, so every pushed command had to work first time; runner compilation and dependency conflicts were the failure mode to avoid.

what_breaks_first.value: A suite whose cases and fixtures are both authored by the system measures agreement with itself, so '12 of 12' says nothing about the attack space it did not write; and the pass claim is not reachable at all here - no repository, workflow URL or run id is linked. The honest next step for a clone is an external corpus of real malicious samples with a published miss rate.

what_it_does.value: Analyses binaries and payloads, classifies them against a fixed set of attack vectors, and reports a verdict per scenario; positioned as the drift-catching layer of a larger audit platform.

what_it_is.value: A Rust validator that classifies payloads against twelve hand-written attack scenarios, regenerated by a fixture generator and run on every commit by CI.

what_to_steal.value: gen_fixtures.rs as a test *generator*: emit the clean and adversarial cases from the same spec the validator consumes, then let CI rebuild the whole matrix on every commit. It makes a regression impossible to hide and costs one file.

adversarial-compliance-matrix.worth_note: The part worth keeping is the smallest credible security demo there is: a fixture generator plus a fixed scenario matrix wired into CI, so the artifact is a run rather than a slide. It is merged into the sibling submission because both pages describe one platform by one author, and the split version publishes twice the entries for half the evidence.
